summary.text: Jeff Haggit, a Constitution Party candidate and retired electrician and instrumentation technician from Mountain View, Wyoming, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the open at-large U.S. House seat in Wyoming to Chuck Gray.
He has served as state chair and is currently vice-chairman of the Constitution Party of Wyoming, and he had also run for the same seat in 2020 and 2024.

paragraphs.text: Haggit was born in Midland, Michigan, and grew up in farm country; he has lived in Wyoming for about 50 years and in Mountain View for 22.
He graduated from Western Wyoming College in 1978.

According to his questionnaire answers, he retired from the TATA trona processing facility in southwest Wyoming after almost 49 years as an electrician and instrumentation technician, and he also served as a trustee of the workers' Accident and Illness fund.

Haggit has served as state chairman of the Constitution Party of Wyoming and currently describes himself as its vice-chairman. He is also a member of the United Way of Southwest Wyoming's Uinta Advisory Council and a 2016 graduate of the Uinta County Leadership Institute.
He ran for Wyoming's U.S. House seat as the Constitution Party candidate in 2020, receiving 7,905 votes (2.9%), and again in 2024, receiving 5,362 votes (2.1%).
He received 4.3% of the vote to Chuck Gray's 54.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
